headline: Fresh World Bank support pushes Bangladesh's reserves above $32bn
summary: BPM6 reserves reached $32.47 billion, while gross reserves exceeded $37 billion for the first time in 43 months.
details: Bangladesh's foreign currency reserves have climbed above $32 billion, extending a steady recovery driven by robust remittance inflows and international support.
At the close of business on Monday, reserves stood at $32.47 billion under the IMF's BPM6 accounting method, according to Bangladesh Bank Executive Director Arief Hossain Khan.
The increase was bolstered by $667.1 million in loans and grants from the International Development Association (IDA) of the World Bank.
Gross reserves have now exceeded $37 billion for the first time in nearly 43 months, marking a significant milestone in the recovery process.
The steady rise has been driven by strong remittance inflows, with $3.43 billion sent home in May alone, up 15.34 percent from a year earlier.
In the first 13 days of June, expatriates sent home $1.36 billion, pushing total remittances for the current fiscal year above $24 billion.
The central bank has also actively purchased US dollars from commercial banks, buying $101 million in June through auctions, totaling $6.42 billion for the outgoing fiscal year.
Foreign exchange reserves are a key indicator of economic strength, having previously fallen to around $20 billion before the 2024 mass uprising.
While export earnings have weakened, the combination of remittance inflows and World Bank support continues to support the reserves.

headline_marked: Veon proposes [[$1 billion investment initiative]] in Bangladesh
headline: Veon proposes $1 billion investment initiative in Bangladesh
summary: The parent company of Banglalink aims to boost the digital economy with an immediate commitment of $250 million and a focus on AI and digital banking.
details: Veon, the parent company of Banglalink, has proposed a $1 billion investment initiative titled "Invest in Bangladesh NOW!", with an immediate commitment of $250 million.
The proposal was discussed during a meeting between Prime Minister Tarique Rahman and Veon Chairman Augie Fabela at the Prime Minister's Office in Jatiya Sangsad Bhaban.

The initiative, a joint public-private proposal with the Ministry of Post, Telecommunications and ICT, focuses on next-generation digital infrastructure, AI, digital banking, and mobile financial services.
Beyond its own investment, Veon plans to use its global network to attract other international investors to Bangladesh's growing digital economy.
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman urged Banglalink to make smartphones more affordable and reduce internet prices to ensure digital inclusion for all socioeconomic backgrounds.
Veon has also expressed interest in a strategic combination with state-owned mobile operator Teletalk and a possible acquisition of Nagad from the Bangladesh Post Office.
The company has already applied for a digital bank license and received a no-objection certificate from Bangladesh Bank to operate as a payment service provider.
Over the past two decades, Veon has invested more than $2.5 billion in Bangladesh and contributed over $4 billion to the national exchequer.
caption:
A $1 billion boost for Bangladesh's digital future? Veon is proposing a massive investment initiative to transform the digital economy.

Veon, the parent company of Banglalink, has proposed a $1 billion investment initiative titled "Invest in Bangladesh NOW!", with an immediate commitment of $250 million.

The proposal was discussed during a meeting between Prime Minister Tarique Rahman and Veon Chairman Augie Fabela at the Prime Minister's Office in Jatiya Sangsad Bhaban.

The initiative, a joint public-private proposal with the Ministry of Post, Telecommunications and ICT, focuses on next-generation digital infrastructure, AI, digital banking, and mobile financial services.

Beyond its own investment, Veon plans to use its global network to attract other international investors to Bangladesh's growing digital economy.

Prime Minister Tarique Rahman urged Banglalink to make smartphones more affordable and reduce internet prices to ensure digital inclusion for all socioeconomic backgrounds.

Veon has also expressed interest in a strategic combination with state-owned mobile operator Teletalk and a possible acquisition of Nagad from the Bangladesh Post Office.

The company has already applied for a digital bank license and received a no-objection certificate from Bangladesh Bank to operate as a payment service provider.

Over the past two decades, Veon has invested more than $2.5 billion in Bangladesh and contributed over $4 billion to the national exchequer.
